title: Elastic sequence clustering and runtime-aware pad minimization for prefill/decoding
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal: reduce padded tokens and per-token cost by creating an elastic, low-overhead sequence-length clustering layer that informs runtime batching and kernel selection across prefill and decode phases. This ticket implements an "elastic sequence clustering" component that consumes an online sequence-length histogram and outputs cluster assignments for incoming requests. Each cluster gets a tailored batching and kernel selection policy (quantized vs full precision, flash attention vs fallback kernels, prefill buffer sizing). The system prioritizes prefill coalescing and decode scheduling to avoid unnecessary prefix padding during decode.

Why: Static bucketing causes large padding overhead when request length distribution shifts or when the mix of short/long requests is bursty. Previous work (see ENG-62045, ENG-49872) showed significant opportunity but left runtime cluster churn and cross-tenant fairness unsolved. This design targets low-friction rollout to Dedicated pools first and aims for a measurable reduction in padded-token-rate while preserving p95 latency SLOs.

Success metrics (observable): average padding_ratio <= previous - 12% (aim 15-20% improvement), cost-per-token reduction > 10% on mixed workloads, p95 latency not to regress by more than 5% at steady state, cluster switching overhead <= 2% CPU/time cost on scheduling path.

Scope: algorithm and runtime scheduler changes only (no model architecture changes). Includes: online histogram + decayed counters, centroid-based cluster formation with hysteresis and TTLs, per-cluster kernel cost lookup table, prefill coalescer that groups compatible prefixes temporally, KV-cache safety checks for prefill coalescing, fairness weight to avoid starving long-running requests.

Out of scope: user-facing console UX changes, autoscaling policies, and private deployment packaging (follow-up tickets will cover those).
acceptance_criteria: Cluster assignment latency on critical path < 150us (median) in 80% of samples
Canary deployment on 2 Dedicated GPU pools shows padding_ratio delta <= -12% compared to baseline within 72 hours
No regression in p95 decode latency beyond 5% under mixed synthetic traffic (short/long/very-long) using perf harness
Automated integration tests for KV-cache safety when prefill coalescing is enabled
implementation_notes: Algorithm: maintain per-worker exponential-decay histogram of observed request lengths (buckets: 8/16/32/64/128/256/512+). Run lightweight centroid formation every 500ms with hysteresis; don't emit new cluster config unless a cluster reduces expected pad-bytes by >= 3% after accounting for scheduling overhead.

Cost model: offline profiled kernel cost table keyed by (model_arch, seqlen, quantization_level, attention_impl). Server picks kernel for cluster by minimizing estimated ms/token subject to memory headroom buffer.

Prefill coalescer: for prefill-window T (configurable, default 12ms), coalesce requests that map to the same cluster and have compatible KV-cache keys. Assign priority weights for decode-sensitive routes (from route metadata) to break ties.

KV-cache safety: disallow coalescing when requests have incompatible KV lifetimes or identical user-scoped keys that would change semantics. Provide a debug flag to log prevented coalesces for initial canary diagnostics.

Attention optimization: prefer FlashAttention where supported; when cluster predicted seqlen distribution exceeds kernel memory threshold, choose 'chunked-attention' fallback to lower memory blowup at cost of some throughput.
Hysteresis & TTL: cluster TTL 30s by default; require 2 consecutive cluster-change windows to flip an existing long-lived cluster to avoid oscillation under bursty traffic.

Telemetry: emit cluster_id, cluster_seqlen_p50/p95, chosen_kernel, pad_bytes_saved_estimate, coalesce_hit_rate, cluster_switch_count; wire these to /dashboards/runtime/elastic-clustering for canary monitoring.
Backpressure: when queue length grows beyond threshold, degrade cluster sensitivity (collapse to broader clusters) to favor latency stability over pad savings.
Testing: unit tests for centroid math, integration perf tests with synthetic Pareto and bimodal length distributions, and staged canary with consumer-facing routes simulated via perf-harness.
Edge cases: ensure deterministic cluster selection for pinned requests (customer-specified model pins) and maintain strong isolation between tenants in Dedicated pools.
decision_log: 2025-11-03: Chose centroid-based clustering (lightweight k-means with k adaptive) over pure quantile bucketing to better exploit multimodal distributions (decision by Miguel, Aisha, and Priya).
2025-11-05: Opted for 500ms re-evaluation window and 30s cluster TTL after measuring oscillation in 100ms window tests (tradeoff: some stale clusters vs scheduling churn).
2025-11-08: Decided to perform kernel cost lookup at cluster formation time to avoid per-request cost computation on hot path; store chosen kernel in cluster metadata.

linked_artifacts: Related Linear: ENG-62045 (microbatch morphing runtime-driven seqlen cluster), ENG-49872 (kernel-aware routing)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: cluster oscillation under heavy traffic churn causing scheduling overhead and potential p95 regressions. Mitigation: hysteresis, TTLs, and collapsing to coarse clusters under load.
Risk: unfairness across tenants when short requests dominate and take batching slots. Mitigation: tenant-weighted coalescing and prefill priority labels from request metadata.

Risk: incorrectly coalescing requests with incompatible KV-caches leading to stale/misplaced KV reads. Mitigation: conservative default disallow, enterprise opt-in for aggressive coalescing, and thorough integration tests.
